problems.title: Phase A — measure before anything is cut or built
problems.body: Gates every other phase. The cut list is an argument until these four land. Publish each result as a Finding with --measured-at.

problems.title: DONE: opt-in local command telemetry
problems.body:
LANDED 2026-10-19 on branch worktree-agent-ad7b3e587b72a31da, gate green (GATE_EXIT=0, 57 test binaries). Not merged.

.jj/jjj-meta/.telemetry.jsonl, one JSON object per line: {ts, command, subcommand, ms}. Enabled only by JJJ_TELEMETRY=1. Disabled costs ONE GETENV, 83ns - no stat, no file creation. Enabled ~120us, about 1% of a 26ms invocation. 16 concurrent processes each append one intact line via a single write_all to an O_APPEND file; no lock, so concurrent agents never serialise.

Verified independently, not taken on report: push.rs copies a hard allowlist into a separate .jj/jjj-sync workspace (same mechanism that keeps automation.toml local); fetch.rs::classify is an allowlist ending _ => Target::Skip; telemetry.rs uses only ArgMatches::subcommand with no get_one/value_of/values_of anywhere, so a title, body, id or path cannot reach the file even in principle.

LIMITATION THAT LANDS ON A4: an invocation clap REJECTS is never recorded (clap prints and exits before main). Harmless for A1's purpose; the opposite for A4, where a rejected command is exactly the 'what did the agent reach for' signal. A4 must capture those from its own harness.

problems.title: DONE: cache-off benchmark; criterion did not fire by 11%
problems.body:
RAN 2026-10-19 on branch worktree-agent-ae5ed5897bca03ebf. Cache-off prime p50 at 5,000 entities is 451ms against the 500ms line (452ms on a 200-rep re-run). CRITERION DID NOT FIRE.

But: margin is 11%, the p99 of that cell is 604ms (already over), and the knee is exactly at the gate - ~82us/entity at 5K, ~114us at 25K, so 500ms lands at 4,500-5,500 entities. The threshold sat on the inflection by coincidence.

NOT comfortably fast at 25,000: 2.88s cache-off. What actually strengthens the deletion is that prime misses 500ms WITH the cache at 25K too (856ms). The cache's whole value window is ~2,000-25,000 entities and the observed corpus is 52.

DECOMPOSITION MATTERS MORE THAN THE VERDICT: emptying the event shards (75,004 -> 4) moved prime 2% at 5K and 0% at 25K. The event log is NOT the cost; per-entity parse_frontmatter is. The future lever is lazy/partial frontmatter decode or a per-file hash skip, NOT an index over events.

Composed with A3: both found the cost is turning bytes into structs. Predicted cache-off prime at 5,000 entities after Phase C: ~455ms at 1 op/entity (passes), ~870ms at 100 (fails), ~4.2s at 1,000 (fails badly). A2's green light does not survive Phase C.

problems.title: DONE: op-log replay cost curve measured
problems.body:
RAN 2026-10-19. Kill criterion DID NOT FIRE: 0.92ms parse+fold p99 at 1000 ops/entity, 9.1ms with one object read per pack, against the 50ms line. Margin held at 128B and 8000B bodies.

Four findings that outrank the verdict:
1. Replay is free (77ns/op); DESERIALISATION is the cost (0.84us/op, 11x more). A snapshot must store materialised state, not a memoised fold.
2. Growth is exactly linear, no knee. What degrades first is SIZE: 1,090x amplification at 1000 ops (354KiB log vs 0.9KiB state), 1.7GB at 5000 entities.
3. The dominant cost is C3's layout decision, not C9's compaction. One object per pack adds ~21us open/read/close = 8x the parse cost, and moves the 50ms crossing from ~17,000 ops to ~4,700. Free if decided before C3 is written.
4. The operating point is UNMEASURED and is the real gap: observed usage is ~1 op/entity, and neither live corpus even has a lamport field. A4 must record ops/entity.

Spike in tools/spike-oplog/ on branch worktree-agent-a9227d7fafdb5564a, not merged.

problems.title: Swarm trial restricted to the seven verbs
problems.body:
Agents told only prime, next, query, create, edit, escalate, doctor exist. See the August 2026 trial notes for harness traps that cost whole runs.

Done when every reach outside the seven is logged with what it wanted. Each distinct reach becomes a Problem, not an automatic feature.

TWO MANDATORY ADDITIONS from A1 and A3:
1. Capture clap-REJECTED invocations from the harness, not from .telemetry.jsonl - telemetry structurally cannot see them, and they are the most interesting rows.
2. RECORD OPERATIONS PER ENTITY. A3 produced the replay curve but nothing says where on it a swarm sits; observed usage is ~1 op/entity and neither live corpus has a lamport field. This number decides whether C9's threshold is ever approached and whether B1's derived index is sized right. LARGEST REMAINING UNKNOWN IN THE PLAN.

Blocked here: needs a container fleet and a real trial harness.

problems.title: Phase B — cut the SQLite cache first
problems.body: Counter-intuitive ordering, and load-bearing. CACHE_FAITHFUL means each model field costs six coordinated steps: DDL, SCHEMA_VERSION bump, requires_rebuild migration, upsert, positional decoder, DbEntity::COLUMNS. Phase C rewrites the model wholesale, so building the op-log while the cache mirrors every field doubles the work and invites a silent decode drift.

problems.title: Reduce src/db/ to a minimal derived index (not delete)
problems.body:
CORRECTED after A3. B1 and Phase C are NOT independent and the first draft treated them as if they were.

An op-log makes a single entity read 88x more expensive at 1000 ops than today's state-based read, crossing over at ~10 ops/entity. A2 measures cache-off prime against TODAY's markdown storage, so A2's green light does not survive Phase C.

Worse: prime must read EVERY entity to compute the ready front even though its output is constant in corpus size. A2's own kill line (500ms / 5000 entities = 100us/entity) allows only ~34 ops/entity. No swarm sits below 34 edits per problem. Per-entity snapshots (C9) do not fix this; prime needs a CORPUS-LEVEL materialised read path.

That is a cache. Confirmed independently: a Rust reimplementation of git-bug WITHOUT a cache lists 48,889 issues in ~5s vs ~400ms for git-bug WITH its cache, and its author attributes the gap to the missing cache layer. git-bug needs a cache BECAUSE it has an op-log. The design note recommended adopting the op-log and deleting the cache; those undercut each other.

SO: strip src/db/ to a minimal derived index - id, status, parent, lamport, assignee, materialised body - and delete the rest (FTS, semantic search, the 16-column mirror, the migration ladder). Most of the LOC saving survives, and most of the CACHE_FAITHFUL relief, since far fewer fields are mirrored. The index must be declared DERIVED and REBUILDABLE, never a source of truth. Phase C owns keeping it in step.

The effort argument for B-before-C still holds: a smaller mirror makes the C rewrite cheaper. What changed is that the cache cannot be deleted, so the 8-10K headline needs revisiting once this is scoped.

problems.title: Remove src/embeddings.rs
problems.body: 495 LOC. Depends on B1.

problems.title: Fold search into query
problems.body:
222 LOC. The real content of this unit, found by A2: jjj search has NO fallback and silently becomes O(corpus) per invocation - with no usable cache it calls load_from_markdown, a full rebuild, on EVERY query. Measured 521ms at 2,000 entities; search.rs's own comment puts it near 10s at 25,000. It does not fail, it goes quietly quadratic in a swarm.

Also unnamed anywhere in the original plan: critique list --search and finding list --search have the same hard dependency, and semantic similarity (jjj search p/<id>) needs the embeddings table that B2 removes.

problems.title: Phase C — the op-log substrate (keystone)
problems.body: Modelled on git-bug's verified data model. Replaces state+pick_side, which resolves lossily: the loser survives only in jj history, documented in 401ec92. C4 -> C7 -> C8 is the project bottleneck.

problems.title: Operation and OperationPack types with serialization
Lamport handling plus the DAG clock invariant
problems.body:
git-bug refuses any commit whose clock is not lower than its child's, making clock abuse structurally impossible. jjj currently caps witnessing at a 1,000,000 jump, which is a heuristic. Implement the structural check; keep the cap as a second line.

Done when a pack claiming an out-of-DAG-order clock is REFUSED, not clamped.

problems.title: Decide pack layout, then store packs on the jjj bookmark
problems.body:
A3 found this is the largest FREE lever in the phase - free before the code is written, expensive after.

One git object per pack puts ~21us of open/read/close in front of every pack: 8x the parse cost, and it moves the 50ms crossing from ~17,000 ops down to ~4,700.

The write side has the same variable and is UNMEASURED: 1000 ops/entity at 3 ops/pack is 333 new git objects per entity - 17,000 across the real 52-entity corpus, 1.7M at 5000 entities. Plausibly the same thing as the open sync-delta latency item in the bench memory.

Done when a written decision exists among one-object-per-pack, one-object-per-entity and packfile, with read AND write cost stated for each, made BEFORE any storage code lands.

problems.title: Deterministic replay with pack-id tie-break
problems.body: Depends on C2 and C3.

problems.title: Conflicted value as a first-class state
problems.body:
The synthesis of both founding insights. Concurrent edits to one field produce a conflicted VALUE, not a winner: it appears in prime, is queryable, any principal may adjudicate it with an argument, and it escalates if nobody does.

Done when two clones edit one body, both sync, neither body is lost or silently chosen, and the problem appears on the ready front needing adjudication.

problems.title: Migrate state-based .md files into the log
problems.body:
Each entity becomes one synthetic import operation carrying current state and the existing lamport value.

Done when every release-corpus fixture migrates and round-trips, and doctor REPORTS any entity that failed rather than skipping it.

problems.title: Adversarial property tests for the log
problems.body:
ASSIGN TO A DIFFERENT AGENT than C1-C5, written against the spec without reading their code. Three properties:
- convergence: any permutation of merge order over the same op set replays to identical state
- no loss: every op ever written is recoverable from the log alone, with no reference to jj history (the property pick_side violates today, and the whole reason for this phase)
- clock abuse: a fabricated clock cannot reorder another principal's operations

This is the gate for the phase. If it cannot be made to pass, C8 does not run.

problems.title: Delete merge.rs and pick_side
problems.body: 1,697 LOC. Depends on C4 and C7.

problems.title: Materialised snapshots and compaction
problems.body:
NO LONGER CONDITIONAL. A3's kill criterion did not fire, so C9 is not needed to unblock C8 - but it is needed for two other reasons A3 surfaced:

1. On-disk growth is 1,090x at 1000 ops/entity (354KiB log vs 0.9KiB state), which is 1.7GB at 5000 entities. Size degrades before latency does.
2. prime reads every entity, which no per-entity threshold fixes.

A SNAPSHOT MUST STORE MATERIALISED STATE, NOT A MEMOISED FOLD. The fold is 77ns/op and free; deserialisation is 0.84us/op and is the entire cost. A memoised fold saves nothing.

Recommended per-entity threshold: 1000 ops. Keeps every layer >=4.7x under the 50ms line on an M1 Ultra, so it survives a 2-3x slower CI runner or cloud vCPU.

C9 and B1's derived index are the same problem from two ends. Whoever takes either should read both.

problems.title: Phase D — the seven verbs
problems.body: Seven parallel agents, but D0 blocks all of them. ~102 leaf operations become ~20.

problems.title: Specify the output contract
problems.body:
One markdown shape per verb that reads well to a human and parses deterministically, plus --json on prime, query, next, create ONLY. The other 49 --json flags go.

Done when a parity harness asserts markdown and JSON carry the same facts for any entity. This is what prevents a recurrence of 1405f17, where --json returned less than the text path.

problems.title: prime: output constant in corpus size
problems.body:
The hard one. The binding constraint on an agent is context window.

Done when prime output byte length varies less than 2x between a 50-entity and a 25,000-entity corpus.

problems.title: query: one grammar over three kinds
problems.body: Absorbs list, search, timeline, events, insights, overlaps, contention and waiting.

problems.title: edit: --if-lamport and exit 13
problems.body: Exit 13 stays reserved for JjjError::Precondition only. beads uses 13 for the same meaning; do not broaden it.

problems.title: escalate with --reply
problems.body: Both halves already exist as of 24f6557.

problems.title: doctor: read-only, exits nonzero on a fault
problems.body: Judgement-gated fixes must be ABSENT, not gated: a tool schema reads as an offer.

problems.title: Collapse transitions into edit --status
problems.body: solution submit/approve/withdraw, problem reopen, critique dismiss and the rest. Guards and events must come from the shared domain layer exactly as plan.rs actions already do. The comment at src/commands/plan.rs:65 explains why a bulk path setting status directly is a hole, and names beads as having it. Do not reintroduce it.

problems.title: Phase E — three nouns
problems.body: Data migration. Sequential with C6.

problems.title: Finding becomes a cited Problem body
problems.body:
Zero findings exist outside tests. The mechanism worth keeping is --cites, which becomes a frontmatter list on all kinds. measured_at from 27e44e2 moves with it.

Done when every corpus finding becomes a cited body with no content lost, and query 'cites:<id>' returns what finding list --problem used to.

problems.title: Milestone survives iff it gains a decline list
problems.body:
NOT a solo-vs-group branch point. The design splits on single-principal vs MULTI-principal, and a swarm is always multi-principal: one human plus twelve agents is thirteen principals. The human count does not reach Phase C.

Keeping a fifth kind is not free - it must migrate into the op-log (C6), render in the panel (F3), appear in query, and be taught in SKILL.md (H1). 'It might be useful' is the reasoning this plan exists to stop. So the test is not headcount:

THE KIND SURVIVES IFF it becomes a commitment recording what is DECLINED - 'this window, these problems, and explicitly not those' - which a tag cannot carry and which the swarm reads in prime. If it stays 'time-based goals grouping problems', it is a tag with extra steps and it goes.

The decline list is the Popperian half: a commitment that does not say what it declines is not falsifiable, and it is what stops a swarm drifting into work that was decided against. A solo operator has no colleague to catch that drift, so this is not a team feature.

Done when either the kind ships with a decline list surfaced by prime, or it is migrated to a tag. Not left as it is.

problems.title: Optional: rename Solution to Attempt, Critique to Objection
problems.body: Better names - Objection makes the veto reading obvious - but it touches every file, every test and SKILL.md. Take it only if A-D came in under budget. If skipped, say so in the changelog rather than leaving the design note and the code disagreeing.

problems.title: Divergence detection across principals
problems.body:
UNCONDITIONAL - not gated on E2. A multi-PRINCIPAL feature, so always live.

rg -i 'variance|divergen|disagree' src/ranking/ src/commands/rank.rs returns NOTHING: the system computes a global aggregate and never surfaces where principals differ. That is backwards. Deciding what to work on is out of band - a meeting, a doc, an argument, someone's judgement - and the aggregate is the part that pretends to decide. What a tool can do that the conversation cannot is arrive with the agenda already computed: which problems are ranked most differently, by whom.

With several humans it names what they disagree about. With one human and a swarm it names WHERE THE AGENTS DISAGREE WITH YOU, which is exactly where scarce human attention belongs. Same code, different population compared.

Per-principal orderings already exist at rankings/{milestone_id}/{user}.json. Build a rank-variance across principals, sorted descending, exposed as query 'contested:true' and a region in the F3 panel. ~50 lines against the 1,293 that G1 extracts.

Done when, given three orderings, it names what they disagree about most and stays silent about what they agree on.

problems.title: Phase F — MCP server and the App panel
problems.body: SEP-1865 went Final 2026-01-26. Can start once D0 lands; must not merge before Gate D.

problems.title: jjj mcp serve: seven tools, visibility-scoped
problems.body: visibility ['model','app'] on the five shared verbs; ['app'] on the human-only acts. The spec says a host MUST REJECT a model-initiated tools/call for a tool lacking 'app', which makes human authority host-enforced rather than an honour system in jjj's own code. Do NOT also implement an is_human policy check - that was the superseded design.

problems.title: Error envelope with a retryable flag
problems.body: Exit 13 has no carrier in an MCP result. Carry it as retryable:true, which the panel renders as 'someone moved this, reload'. Scope the envelope to retryable vs not, nothing more.

problems.title: The ui:// panel, four regions
problems.body:
mime text/html;profile=mcp-app. Regions: ready front, who is on what, open objections, escalations waiting. Zero external domains, so the default default-src 'none' CSP needs no relaxation. D0's markdown is the required text fallback.

State persistence is UNDEFINED in the MCP Apps MVP - do not rely on filters or scroll surviving teardown.

problems.title: App-only tools
problems.body: Answer an escalation; file an objection; approve/reject an attempt. Only these. Do not put resourceUri on a tool with no panel: a UI-linked tool returning only text renders an empty, never-resolving loading box.

problems.title: Stateless-per-call invariant and test
problems.body:
An MCP server is long-lived; jjj is one-shot. The server must re-read from disk every call or it drifts from what other agents and jj git fetch have done. This is also the invariant that keeps Phase B honest.

Done when an external write between two tools/calls is visible to the second, and check-invariants.sh enforces that src/mcp/ caches no entity state.

problems.title: Phase G — deletions
problems.body: Each independent and parallel, all gated on Gate D. One commit per unit.

problems.title: EXTRACT src/ranking/, do not delete
problems.body:
1,293 LOC. An extraction, not a deletion. The budget normalisation (B = max(100, 2*problem_count), so ranking 10 items carries the same influence as ranking 200 - test at scoring.rs:182) is correct work that becomes right again the moment there are several humans. Move it out of the swarm core, keep docs/design/latent-preference-ranking.md, and record in the changelog that it can return as an optional layer.

See also E2 and the portfolio question: what a group actually needs is DISAGREEMENT DETECTION, which this code does not do - rg for variance/divergence/disagree in src/ranking/ returns nothing. It computes an aggregate only.

problems.title: Remove src/tui/
problems.body: 6,790 LOC. Justification in one line: rg 'crate::commands::' src/tui/ returns ZERO matches, while MetadataStore/save_* appear 8x in app/actions/edit.rs, 7x in lifecycle.rs, 7x in create.rs and 6x in app/mod.rs, and next_actions.rs:68 computes its own blocking logic. It is a second implementation of the model, not a view. F3 replaces the interface part.

problems.title: Remove the VS Code extension
problems.body: Parity obligation, zero observed use.

problems.title: Remove src/sync/ (GitHub)
problems.body: 1,878 LOC. query --json piped to gh covers the real need.

problems.title: Remove src/automation.rs
problems.body: 585 LOC. A SECURITY deletion: automation rules produced the RCE fixed in 0.5.1. The swarm's automation is agents polling next, strictly more capable with no shell-template surface. Leave 'jjj automation migrate' in place for one release so an existing automation.toml is reported rather than silently ignored.

problems.title: Rewrite SKILL.md for the seven verbs
problems.body: LAST ON PURPOSE. include_str! means every edit rebuilds the crate and 56 test binaries, and there is a drift test. One pass at the end.

problems.title: Add invariant checks for this plan's lessons
problems.body:
Encode them so the next swarm cannot repeat them:
- no file outside the op-log layer writes storage directly (the G2 bug class)
- no gate step is piped through rg (a pipeline's status becomes ripgrep's, so a green run can sit on top of real clippy errors - this happened)
- exit_code() returns 13 only for Precondition
- src/mcp/ caches no entity state across calls

Also commit scripts/verify-commits.sh if it is not yet in scripts/.

problems.title: Changelog and bump to 0.6.0
problems.body: A breaking release. Say plainly what was removed, that ranking is extracted rather than gone, and that --if-lamport's documented limitation from 401ec92 is now narrower because a lost race no longer discards the loser. DO NOT TAG. DO NOT PUBLISH.

findings.title: Telemetry disabled costs 83 ns: one getenv, no stat, no file
findings.method: 100k-iteration microbenchmark of the disabled path; 16-process concurrent append test; release-mode timing against a 26 ms baseline invocation
findings.body:
Measured 2026-10-19. Disabled: 83 ns, a single getenv of JJJ_TELEMETRY — no stat, no directory probe, no file creation. Enabled: ~120 us, about 1% of a 26 ms invocation. 16 concurrent processes each appended one intact line via a single write_all to an O_APPEND handle with no lock and no interleaving. Records only {ts, command, subcommand, ms}; the module touches ArgMatches::subcommand only, never get_one/value_of/values_of, so entity content cannot leak by construction. Verified independently: push.rs copies a hard allowlist into a separate .jj/jjj-sync workspace and fetch.rs::classify ends in `_ => Target::Skip`, so .telemetry.jsonl cannot reach a remote.

LIMITATION, lands on A4: a clap-rejected invocation is never recorded, because the process exits before any handler runs. That is precisely A4's most interesting signal — the verbs an agent reached for and did not find. A4 must capture it from the harness, not from telemetry.

findings.title: Cache-off prime is 451 ms at 5,000 entities; p99 604 ms is already over
findings.method: tools/bench/cache_off.py, release binary, synthetic corpora at 50/500/5,000/25,000 entities, p50 and p99 over 50 reps (200 on the 5,000 cell); decomposition by emptying event shards
findings.body:
Measured 2026-10-19. Cache-off `prime` p50: 40.8 ms @ 50, 76.8 ms @ 500, 451.4 ms @ 5,000, 2884 ms @ 25,000. Cache-on: 38.8 / 41.7 / 87.0 / 856.3 ms. The 5,000 cell reproduced to 1 ms over 200 reps.

The criterion (p50 < 500 ms @ 5,000) did not fire, but the margin is 11% and that cell's p99 is 604 ms — already past the budget. The cost is ~82 us/entity at 5,000 and ~114 us at 25,000, so 500 ms is crossed at 4,500-5,500 entities: the gate sat on the knee by coincidence.

The result that actually strengthens the deletion is a different one: `prime` misses 500 ms WITH the cache at 25,000 too (856 ms). The cache's whole value window is a corpus of roughly 2,000-25,000 entities, and below 500 entities it is worth under 40 ms. The observed corpus is 52.

DECOMPOSITION: emptying the event shards (75,004 events down to 4) moved `prime` 2% at 5,000 and 0% at 25,000. The event log is not the cost. Per-entity parse_frontmatter is.

findings.title: Op-log replay is free at 77 ns/op; deserialisation at 0.84 us/op is the cost
findings.method: tools/spike-oplog standalone binary (excluded from the workspace), synthetic op-logs at 1/10/100/1,000/5,000 ops per entity, 128 B and 8 KB bodies, p99 over 1,000 trials; separate run with one git object read per pack
findings.body:
Measured 2026-10-19. Parse+fold p99 at 1,000 ops/entity is 0.92 ms against the 50 ms criterion — 54x under. 9.1 ms with one git object read per pack. Holds at both 128 B and 8 KB bodies.

FOUR RESULTS, in descending order of how much they change the plan:

1. Replay is free: 77 ns/op to fold. Deserialisation is the cost at 0.84 us/op — 11x the fold. A snapshot must therefore store MATERIALISED STATE, not a memoised fold; memoising the cheap half saves nothing.

2. Size degrades before time does. Growth is exactly linear with no knee: 1,090x amplification at 1,000 ops, 1.7 GB at 5,000 entities. The op-log's first failure mode is disk, not latency.

3. The dominant cost is C3's layout decision, not C9's compaction. One git object per pack adds ~21 us open/read/close, 8x the parse cost, and moves the 50 ms crossing from ~17,000 ops to ~4,700. Free to decide before the code exists; expensive afterwards. C3 is promoted ahead of C9.

4. The operating point is unmeasured, and that is the real gap. Observed usage is ~1 op/entity: minerva_old has 46 events across 45 problems, and neither live corpus has a `lamport` field at all. This curve becomes a decision only once A4 records ops/entity.

STRUCTURAL HOLE this exposes in the plan, verified independently: `prime` must read every entity to compute the ready front even though its output is constant in corpus size. An op-log makes each read op-proportional — 88x more expensive at 1,000 ops, crossing over at ~10 ops/entity — while A2's kill line implies a 100 us/entity budget, i.e. only ~34 ops/entity. Per-entity snapshots do not fix `prime`; it needs a corpus-level materialised read path, which is a cache. git-bug-rs confirms it from outside: without a cache layer it lists 48,889 issues in ~5 s against ~400 ms for git-bug with one, and its author attributes the gap to the missing cache. git-bug needs a cache BECAUSE it has an op-log.
